delta: # Story 01 — Expired-token 401 retur

ns the reader to sign-in with a session-ended notice (Story: CRM-46)

## Prerequisites

- **IDENTITY-1-WEB**
shipped: `web/src/app/auth-context.tsx` already exposes `signIn`/`signOut`, persists the token under
`support-desk.auth-token`, and wires `setAuthTokenGetter` into `web/src/shared/api/client.ts` (see the `useEffect`

at ~lines 56–58 of `auth-context.tsx`).
- **CRM-30** shipped: `scripts/verify-architecture.mjs` enforces the direction of imports between
`web/src/shared/**` and `web/src/app/**`. Do **not** disable, allow-list, or edit that rule to

satisfy this story.
- **CRM-31** shipped: `t.errors.UNAUTHENTICATED` in `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `ar.ts` reads "Your session has ended.

Sign in again to continue." Reuse verbatim; do not add a second sentence.
- **API side already done.** Per
IDENTITY-1-API, an expired token is already refused with `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` and `identity.test.js` covers "an expired token

is refused". No `api/` change in this story.
- Coordinate with the owner of `web/src/pages/sign-in/SignInPage.tsx`: this story only
**adds** a banner path that shows `t.errors.UNAUTHENTICATED` when the session was terminated by the client; it does **not** alter wrong-password hand

ling (L-29 — kept distinct on purpose).

---

## Story Goal

When any authenticated request in the web app is

refused with `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` because the stored token is no longer accepted, the app must:

1. Clear the persisted session exactly once,

even when several in-flight requests all fail with 401.
2. Land the reader on `/sign-in` exactly once (no redirect lo

op, no flicker).
3. Show the reader `t.errors.UNAUTHENTICATED` ("Your session has ended…") on `/sign-in` so the transition is expl

ained rather than silent.
4. **Not** hijack the 401 that the sign-in request itself returns for a wrong password — that message must remain on scre

en and the (nonexistent) session must not be "cleared".

Explicitly out of scope: silent token refresh, restoring the pre-exp
iry route, any `api/` change, changing the `ApiError` shape, changing the sign-in screen's own error handling or the throttle, and carrying/

disabling any `verify-architecture.mjs` rule.

---

## Context — Read These Files First

ines 4–11). The failure path (`response.ok === false`) throws a fresh `ApiError` at lines 50–55 and is the **only** place a

401 is produced. Any expired-token hook must fire here, not in every call site.
2. `` `web/src/shared/api/errors.ts` `` —

whole file (39 lines). `ApiError` carries `status`, `code`, `requestId`, and optional `fields`. **Do not change this shape.**
3. `` `web/src/app/
auth-context.tsx` `` — whole file (~74 lines). `signIn`/`signOut` are `useCallback`s that mutate `localStorage` and `token` state. `setAuthTokenGetter` is invoked from

a `useEffect` (~lines 56–58). This is the correct place to also register a handler that runs on 401.
4. `` `web/src/shared/hooks/useRequest.ts` `` — whole file (~40 lines). Conf
irms that a non-`ApiError` throw is coerced into an `ApiError({ status: 0, code: 'INTERNAL' })`. The expired-session detection must key

off `status === 401 && code === 'UNAUTHENTICATED'`, not on `status === 401` alone.
5. `` `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` `` (and `ar.ts`) — the `errors.UN

AUTHENTICATED` entry ("Your session has ended. Sign in again to continue.") is the sentence to show on sign-in. Do not add a new key.
6. `` `web/
src/pages/sign-in/SignInPage.tsx` `` and `SignInPage.test.tsx` — read end to end. Find where the wrong-password error is rendered; the session-ended banner is

a **separate, dismissible** element rendered above the form, and must not replace or converge with the wrong-password message (L-29).
7. `

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current:** the
web client throws `ApiError` on 401; nothing observes it. A screen that receives 401 shows a generic error and keeps the (now-wor

thless) token in `localStorage`. The reader is stuck on a broken screen.
- **New:** an expired-token 401 (i.e. any
authenticated request other than the sign-in request itself) clears the session **once** and lands the reader on `/sign-in` **once**, with `t.errors.UNAUTHENTICATED` displayed. Wrong-password 401

on the sign-in request is unchanged.

---

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Wrong-password 401 on sign-in.** Trigger: `POST /api/v1/sign-in` returns `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`. Exp
ected: banner does **not** appear, `sessionEnded` stays `false`, token (already `null`) is not written, form-level error message from
the existing sign-in error path is shown. Enforced at: `client.ts` `suppressSessionExpiry` branch (step

1) and by the sign-in caller passing the flag (step 2).
- **Concurrent 401s from the same dead token.** Trigger: three parallel `request()` calls all reject with `
401 UNAUTHENTICATED`. Expected: `signOut` runs once, `setSessionEnded(true)` runs once (or is idempotent — same visible outcome), one

navigation. Enforced by the `readTokenRef.current === null` guard in `auth-context.tsx` (step 3).
- **401 fires while reader is already on `/sign-in` (session
ended in another tab, then user types).** Expected: `sessionEnded` may flip to `true`, banner appears, no navigation loop because `require-auth`

only guards **protected** routes.
- **`localStorage` throws.** Trigger: private-mode browser or blocked storage. Existing `try/catch` in `readSt
oredToken`/`signIn`/`signOut` already swallows the error; the in-memory `token` still transitions to `null`, so the handler still fires once. No new handling

needed.
- **A non-`ApiError` throw from `useRequest`.** `useRequest.ts` coerces to `ApiError({ status: 0, code: 'INTERNAL
' })` — the expiry handler will not fire (status is 0). Correct: a fetch/network fail

ure is not an expired session.
- **Non-401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` or 401 with a different code.** Handler fires **only**

on `status === 401 && code === 'UNAUTHENTICATED'`. A 403 `FORBIDDEN` (different rule) does not sign out.
- **
Reader clicks the "Sign out" button in `DeskShell`.** `signOut()` (the manual one) clears the token but must **not** set `sessionEnded`; land

ing on `/sign-in` with no banner is the correct UX for a voluntary sign-out.
- **`t.errors.UNAUTHENTICATED`
divergence with wrong-password copy.** L-29: intentionally different. Do not consolidate. Verified by the parity test in `web

/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts` (already existing — keys, not sentences).

## Migration / Rollback

-

No schema or data change; nothing to migrate.
- Rollback is a straight revert of the two touched web source files (`client.ts`, `
auth-context.tsx`) plus the sign-in call site and page render change. A half-applied state (e.g. `client.ts` ship
ped without the auth-context registration) is safe: the default `onUnauthenticated = () => {}` no-op preserves today's behaviour.

---

## Verification Steps

1. **Frontend tests:** `cd web && npm test` — all vitest suites green, including the new ones in the Test Plan.
2. **Frontend builds
:** `cd web && npm run build` — `tsc -b && vite build` must succeed. The web suite does not typecheck under vitest;

this build step is the only proof that the new option type on `request()` and the new fields on `AuthValue` typecheck.
3. **Backend tests (reg

ression):** `cd api && npm test` — no `api/` code changed; suites remain green.
4. **Architecture rule:** `node scripts/verify-architecture.mjs` — must exit 0. This is the check
that fails if any file under `web/src/shared/**` imported from `web/src/app/**`. The chosen design (app regist

appears / does not appear, wrong-password message is shown, no navigation loop.

---

## Design note — chosen dependency shape (one paragraph,

per intake requirement)

The HTTP client owns a single, replaceable handler slot (`setUnauthenticatedHandler(fn)`), anal
ogous to the existing `setAuthTokenGetter(fn)` pattern. The **app layer** registers the handler from `AuthProvider`'s existing `useEffect`; `shared/api/client.ts` imports nothing from `web
/src/app/**`. The handler receives the `ApiError` (not a router or a store) so the client stays free of navigation, React, and storage concerns. The dependency arrow is therefore `
app → shared`, matching the existing token-getter arrow and satisfying `scripts/verify-architecture.mjs` without any allow-list change. The sign-in ca
ller opts out with an explicit `{ suppressSessionExpiry: true }` option so wrong-password 401s never reach the handler, and the option is documented at both
ends with a comment naming IDENTITY-1-API so the next global-401 change reviews this decision inst

ead of re-discovering it.

---

ands the reader on `/sign-in`.
- [ ] The reader sees `t.errors.UNAUTHENTICATED` ("Your session has ended. Sign in again to continue.") on `/sign-in` after a session-expiry red

irect, and does **not** see it after clicking the header sign-out button.
- [ ] A wrong-password 401 from `

POST /api/v1/sign-in` does not clear state, does not navigate, and does not show the session-ended banner.
- [ ] Three concurrent 401s from the same dead token produ

ce **one** state clear and **one** navigation to `/sign-in`.
- [ ] `web/src/shared/api/client.ts` imports nothing from `web/src/app/**`; `node scripts/verify-architec

ture.mjs` exits 0.
- [ ] `cd web && npm test` and `cd web && npm run build` both pass; `cd api && npm test` still passes with no `api/` edits.
- [ ] No committed file m

entions AI assistance (grep in step 5 clean).
- [ ] `t.errors.UNAUTHENTICATED` is reused verbatim in `en.

ts` and `ar.ts`; no new i18n key added; wrong-password sentence remains distinct (L-29).
